render.description: Provides the job configuration object consumed by the selected job implementation.
render.benefits: Makes the root.config configuration boundary explicit.
render.drawbacks: An invalid root.config value stops job configuration or process loading.

render.description: Selects the top-level job implementation that consumes the configuration.
render.benefits: Makes the root.job configuration boundary explicit.
render.drawbacks: An invalid root.job value stops job configuration or process loading.

render.description: Carries optional metadata from the job envelope into each process.
render.benefits: Makes the root.meta configuration boundary explicit.
render.drawbacks: An invalid root.meta value stops job configuration or process loading.

render.description: Names the job and supplies the inherited process name fallback.
render.benefits: Makes the job.name configuration boundary explicit.
render.drawbacks: An invalid job.name value stops job configuration or process loading.

render.description: Defines the nonempty ordered list of processes loaded for the job.
render.benefits: Makes the job.processes configuration boundary explicit.
render.drawbacks: An invalid job.processes value stops job configuration or process loading.

render.description: Selects the registered implementation for each process entry.
render.benefits: Makes the process.type configuration boundary explicit.
render.drawbacks: An invalid process.type value stops job configuration or process loading.

render.description: Selects the device string inherited by extension-job processes.
render.benefits: Allows an extension job to target a specific available compute device.
render.drawbacks: An unavailable or malformed device string prevents the process from running.

render.description: Overrides the inherited job name for one process.
render.benefits: Distinguishes process output folders and timing labels in multi-process jobs.
render.drawbacks: Changing the name also changes name-derived output paths.

render.description: Sets the interval used by process performance logging; zero disables periodic logging.
render.benefits: Can expose timing trends during a long process.
render.drawbacks: Frequent performance logging adds console noise and a small measurement overhead.

render.description: Overrides the inherited TensorBoard log directory for one process.
render.benefits: Keeps TensorBoard event files in a chosen location.
render.drawbacks: A null value disables TensorBoard setup, while an unwritable path fails logging.

render.description: Overrides the inherited root folder used for training artifacts.
render.benefits: Controls where the named process folder and saved configuration are created.
render.drawbacks: The process cannot initialize its output path when no usable folder is supplied.

normalizations.description: A present seed is applied to PyTorch, available CUDA generators, and Python random.

render.description: Overrides the inherited random seed for process initialization.
render.benefits: Helps reproduce initialization and other seeded process behavior.
render.drawbacks: It does not make nondeterministic kernels or every external component deterministic.

render.description: Optional adapter configuration; a present object initializes AdapterConfig.
render.benefits: Enables adapter training alongside or instead of a network.
render.drawbacks: Unsupported adapter/model combinations fail or alter the trainable module set.

render.description: Dataset configuration list passed through preprocessing and DatasetConfig.
render.benefits: Allows one process to combine training and regularization datasets.
render.drawbacks: An empty or incompatible dataset list leaves the trainer without usable training data.

render.description: Optional decorator configuration used by supported Flux models.
render.benefits: Enables decorator-token training when the model supports it.
render.drawbacks: The process rejects decorator configuration for non-Flux models.

render.description: Enables LoRM extraction behavior in the process.
render.benefits: Allows low-rank module extraction for the LoRM workflow.
render.drawbacks: It changes network construction and is not appropriate for ordinary LoRA runs.

render.description: Optional embedding configuration used to create trainable tokens.
render.benefits: Enables embedding training within the diffusion trainer.
render.drawbacks: Trigger and token settings must be compatible with the selected text encoders.

render.description: Optional sampling overrides used only for the initial sample.
render.benefits: Lets the first baseline sample differ from recurring samples.
render.drawbacks: A second sample configuration increases the chance of incomparable evaluation settings.

render.description: Optional training-guidance configuration.
render.benefits: Enables class-targeted guidance when the process supports it.
render.drawbacks: Guidance adds computation and requires compatible prompts and targets.

render.description: Logging configuration forwarded to LoggingConfig.
render.benefits: Controls console, UI, and external experiment logging.
render.drawbacks: External logging can add latency or require credentials.

render.description: Chooses the LoRM extraction rule.
render.benefits: Supports fixed, threshold, ratio, or quantile rank selection.
render.drawbacks: The wrong rule or parameter can retain too much or too little information.

render.description: Supplies the numeric parameter interpreted by the selected LoRM extraction mode.
render.benefits: Tunes how aggressively LoRM components are retained.
render.drawbacks: Its meaning changes with lorm_extract_mode and unsuitable values degrade extraction.

normalizations.description: The process overwrites model.dtype with the parsed training dtype before ModelConfig is created.

render.description: Model configuration forwarded to ModelConfig after dtype synchronization.
render.benefits: Selects and configures the base diffusion model.
render.drawbacks: An incompatible model configuration prevents loading or changes memory requirements.

render.description: Optional network configuration forwarded to NetworkConfig.
render.benefits: Enables LoRA, LyCORIS, and related trainable network types.
render.drawbacks: Network shape choices affect capacity, memory use, and checkpoint compatibility.

render.description: Recurring sample configuration forwarded to SampleConfig.
render.benefits: Provides comparable progress images or media during training.
render.drawbacks: Sampling pauses training work and consumes memory and compute.

render.description: Checkpoint configuration forwarded to SaveConfig.
render.benefits: Controls checkpoint cadence and serialization.
render.drawbacks: Frequent or retained checkpoints consume storage and time.

render.description: Enables a PyTorch profiler around the training loop.
render.benefits: Can identify expensive operations during diagnosis.
render.drawbacks: Profiling adds substantial overhead and verbose output.

render.description: Training configuration forwarded to TrainConfig.
render.benefits: Controls the optimizer-step and precision behavior of the process.
render.drawbacks: Invalid combinations can fail validation or produce poor training behavior.

render.description: Defines a process-level trigger inherited by datasets and sample prompts when applicable.
render.benefits: Keeps concept activation consistent across training data and evaluation prompts.
render.drawbacks: An unsuitable or common trigger can entangle the learned concept with existing vocabulary.

normalizations.description: A present environment value is stripped of surrounding whitespace before use.

interactions.description: UI job status integration is active only when the configured database path exists as well.

render.description: Carries the server-assigned job identifier into a diffusion trainer process.
render.benefits: Links process status and logs to the matching UI job record.
render.drawbacks: Without a matching server job and database the process runs without UI-trainer status integration.

interactions.description: UI job status integration also requires a present server job identifier.

render.description: Points the diffusion trainer at the SQLite database used for UI job status.
render.benefits: Allows a launched process to report progress and stop state to the local UI database.
render.drawbacks: A missing path disables UI-trainer integration; an incorrect existing database can target the wrong state store.

render.description: Selects the dtype used when checkpoint tensors are serialized.
render.benefits: Can reduce checkpoint size or preserve higher precision.
render.drawbacks: Low-precision formats can lose detail, and unsupported dtype strings fail downstream.

render.description: Marks a newly created Hugging Face repository private when hub upload is enabled.
render.benefits: Keeps uploaded training artifacts access-controlled.
render.drawbacks: Private repositories require authenticated access for later downloads.

render.description: Names the Hugging Face repository that receives uploaded checkpoints.
render.benefits: Routes artifacts to a stable remote repository.
render.drawbacks: A missing or unauthorized repository identifier makes hub upload fail.

render.description: Limits how many numbered step checkpoints remain after cleanup.
render.benefits: Bounds checkpoint disk usage during long runs.
render.drawbacks: A small limit removes older recovery points.

render.description: Uploads saved output to the configured Hugging Face repository after training.
render.benefits: Publishes or backs up the resulting artifacts automatically.
render.drawbacks: Requires credentials and network access and can expose artifacts if privacy is misconfigured.

render.description: Sets the optimizer-step interval between numbered checkpoints.
render.benefits: Creates recovery and comparison points during training.
render.drawbacks: Short intervals interrupt training more often and consume more storage.

render.description: Chooses safetensors output or a Diffusers directory.
render.benefits: Matches the artifact layout to downstream tooling.
render.drawbacks: Diffusers output uses multiple files, while safetensors may not fit every full-model workflow.

render.description: Sets the optimizer-step interval between metric log updates.
render.benefits: Balances metric visibility against logging overhead.
render.drawbacks: Very frequent updates add output and external-logger traffic.

render.description: Names the external experiment project used by configured loggers.
render.benefits: Groups related training runs in experiment tracking.
render.drawbacks: Changing it can fragment runs across multiple projects.

render.description: Overrides the run name sent to experiment logging.
render.benefits: Makes runs easier to identify and compare.
render.drawbacks: Duplicate or vague names make experiment history harder to interpret.

render.description: Enables metric delivery through the toolkit UI logger.
render.benefits: Shows training metrics in the local job interface.
render.drawbacks: It depends on the UI job integration and adds logging work.

render.description: Enables Weights & Biases experiment logging.
render.benefits: Provides remote metric history and run comparison.
render.drawbacks: Requires the dependency, credentials, and network access.

render.description: Enables verbose logger output.
render.benefits: Provides more diagnostic context while troubleshooting.
render.drawbacks: Produces substantially noisier logs.

render.description: Scales adapter or ControlNet conditioning during generated samples.
render.benefits: Lets evaluation match the intended conditioning strength.
render.drawbacks: Excessive conditioning can dominate the prompt or amplify artifacts.

render.description: Enables classifier-free-guidance normalization for models that implement it.
render.benefits: Can reduce overexposed guided samples on supported models.
render.drawbacks: It is model-specific and can change sample comparability.

render.description: Supplies auxiliary numeric conditioning values to adapters that consume them.
render.benefits: Enables evaluation of adapters trained with extra conditioning channels.
render.drawbacks: The value count must match the adapter expectation.

normalizations.description: When num_frames is greater than one, non-WebP formats are changed to animated WebP.

interactions.description: Multiple frames force animated WebP output.

render.description: Chooses the image or animation file extension for samples.
render.benefits: Matches sample output to quality and animation needs.
render.drawbacks: Lossy JPEG can hide detail, while animated output is larger.

render.description: Sets playback frames per second for animated samples.
render.benefits: Controls the review speed of generated video samples.
render.drawbacks: It changes playback timing rather than the generated frame content.

render.description: Rescales classifier-free guidance to limit overexposure.
render.benefits: Can retain guidance while moderating extreme predictions.
render.drawbacks: Unsupported pipelines may ignore it and aggressive values alter prompt adherence.

render.description: Sets classifier-free guidance strength for recurring samples.
render.benefits: Controls how strongly samples follow the prompt.
render.drawbacks: High values can oversaturate or reduce natural variation.

render.description: Sets the requested sample height in pixels.
render.benefits: Lets evaluation use a model-appropriate aspect ratio.
render.drawbacks: Large heights increase memory and generation time and may be rounded by the model.

render.description: Defines the shared negative prompt, with false acting as the disabled sentinel.
render.benefits: Keeps unwanted traits consistently discouraged across samples.
render.drawbacks: A broad negative prompt can suppress desired content.

render.description: Scales the trained network while rendering samples.
render.benefits: Makes it possible to compare weaker or stronger adapter influence.
render.drawbacks: A multiplier unlike deployment strength can misrepresent training progress.

interactions.description: Multiple frames force the format to animated WebP.

render.description: Sets the number of frames generated for each sample.
render.benefits: Enables temporal evaluation for video-capable models.
render.drawbacks: More frames increase memory and generation time.

render.description: Sets the denoising fraction where an available refiner takes over.
render.benefits: Balances base-model composition and refiner detail.
render.drawbacks: An unsuitable handoff can create discontinuities or weak refinement.

render.description: Sets the optimizer-step interval between recurring sample batches.
render.benefits: Provides regular visual progress checks.
render.drawbacks: Short intervals pause training frequently.

render.description: Delays recurring sampling until the configured training step.
render.benefits: Avoids spending time on very early samples.
render.drawbacks: A late start can hide early divergence.

render.description: Sets the denoising step count used for each sample.
render.benefits: Trades sample speed for iterative refinement.
render.drawbacks: Many steps slow evaluation and may not help the selected sampler.

render.description: Selects the sampler used for progress generation.
render.benefits: Allows evaluation with a sampler appropriate to the model.
render.drawbacks: An unsupported sampler fails generation and sampler changes reduce comparability.

render.description: Sets the starting sample seed.
render.benefits: Makes recurring evaluations reproducible.
render.drawbacks: A single seed can hide variation or seed-specific failure.

render.description: Advances the seed between recurring sample events.
render.benefits: Shows progress across varied latent inputs.
render.drawbacks: Changing latents makes step-to-step visual comparison less direct.

render.description: Sets the requested sample width in pixels.
render.benefits: Lets evaluation use a model-appropriate aspect ratio.
render.drawbacks: Large widths increase memory and generation time and may be rounded by the model.

normalizations.description: Legacy prompts strings are converted in order to sample objects containing a prompt field.

aliases.migration: Convert each prompt string to a samples list item with a prompt key; samples is used when both forms are supplied.

render.description: Defines per-item prompts and optional generation overrides for recurring evaluation.
render.benefits: Supports several fixed evaluation cases with independent seeds, sizes, and controls.
render.drawbacks: Large lists lengthen every sampling event; legacy prompts cannot express per-item overrides.

render.description: Selects which control input slot this sample item addresses.
render.benefits: Targets the intended control stream for multi-control models.
render.drawbacks: An index unsupported by the model can select no useful control.

render.description: Sets the primary control image for this sample item.
render.benefits: Evaluates conditioning against a fixed reference input.
render.drawbacks: A missing or incompatible image prevents meaningful controlled evaluation.

interactions.description: When omitted, this item uses sample.item.ctrl_img.

render.description: Sets control image slot one, falling back to the primary control image.
render.benefits: Supports models with explicitly numbered control inputs.
render.drawbacks: Duplicated or misordered control images can obscure which condition is active.

render.description: Sets the optional second control image.
render.benefits: Exercises a model's second control condition.
render.drawbacks: It has no effect for models without that control slot.

render.description: Sets the optional third control image.
render.benefits: Exercises a model's third control condition.
render.drawbacks: It has no effect for models without that control slot.

render.description: Enables classifier-free-guidance normalization for this item.
render.benefits: Allows one model-specific evaluation item to use normalized guidance.
render.drawbacks: It changes output characteristics and is unsupported by many models.

interactions.description: When omitted, this item uses sample.fps.

render.description: Overrides animation playback rate for this item.
render.benefits: Tests a different playback rate without changing every sample.
render.drawbacks: It changes playback timing, not generated motion.

interactions.description: When omitted, this item uses sample.guidance_scale.

render.description: Overrides classifier-free guidance strength for this item.
render.benefits: Tests prompt adherence at an item-specific strength.
render.drawbacks: Different strengths make direct visual comparisons less controlled.

interactions.description: When omitted, this item uses sample.height.

render.description: Overrides output height for this item.
render.benefits: Supports fixed evaluation at multiple aspect ratios.
render.drawbacks: Larger sizes increase generation memory and time.

interactions.description: When omitted, this item uses sample.neg.

render.description: Overrides the shared negative prompt for this item.
render.benefits: Targets item-specific unwanted traits.
render.drawbacks: A broad negative prompt can suppress intended content.

normalizations.description: A string value is converted to float; conversion failure prints a warning and uses 1.0.

interactions.description: When omitted, this item uses sample.network_multiplier.

render.description: Overrides trained-network strength for this item.
render.benefits: Compares the learned effect at a chosen multiplier.
render.drawbacks: A deployment-mismatched value can misrepresent progress.

interactions.description: When omitted, this item uses sample.num_frames.

render.description: Overrides generated frame count for this item.
render.benefits: Evaluates a specific temporal length.
render.drawbacks: More frames increase generation memory and time.

render.description: Sets the positive prompt for this sample item.
render.benefits: Creates a stable qualitative evaluation target.
render.drawbacks: A missing prompt is omitted from the legacy prompts view and may not produce a useful evaluation.

interactions.description: When omitted, this item uses sample.sample_steps.

render.description: Overrides denoising steps for this item.
render.benefits: Tests a chosen quality/speed point.
render.drawbacks: Many steps slow sampling and can reduce comparability.

render.description: Sets an optional fixed seed; null requests automatic seed selection.
render.benefits: Supports either exact repeatability or automatic variation.
render.drawbacks: Automatic seeds make repeated progress samples harder to compare.

interactions.description: When omitted, this item uses sample.width.

render.description: Overrides output width for this item.
render.benefits: Supports fixed evaluation at multiple aspect ratios.
render.drawbacks: Larger sizes increase generation memory and time.

render.description: Enables LoRM attachment to eligible convolution modules.
render.benefits: Extends extraction beyond linear layers when convolution adaptation is needed.
render.drawbacks: Adds trainable capacity, memory use, and larger extracted output.

render.description: Chooses the default rank-extraction rule for LoRM modules.
render.benefits: Controls whether rank is selected by count, threshold, ratio, or quantile.
render.drawbacks: The same numeric parameter has different meaning under each mode.

interactions.description: Its interpretation is selected by extract_mode.

render.description: Supplies the default numeric argument for the selected extraction mode.
render.benefits: Tunes the compression/retention tradeoff.
render.drawbacks: An unsuitable value can discard useful components or retain excessive rank.

normalizations.description: Each module rule is merged over the top-level extraction mode, parameter, and threshold defaults before parsing.

render.description: Defines ordered module-name matching rules that override LoRM extraction defaults.
render.benefits: Allows different rank extraction for distinct module groups.
render.drawbacks: Broad or misordered patterns can apply an unintended override.

render.description: Sets the default parameter-count threshold used when selecting eligible modules.
render.benefits: Skips modules below the chosen size boundary.
render.drawbacks: A high threshold can exclude layers needed by the concept.

normalizations.description: Matching retries after replacing dots in the contains expression with underscores.

render.description: Matches module names; pipe-separated pieces must all occur, with a second check using underscores for dots.
render.benefits: Targets extraction settings to a chosen family of module names.
render.drawbacks: A broad pattern can affect unintended modules; a nonmatching pattern is silently unused.

normalizations.description: LoRMConfig first fills an omitted module override from the corresponding top-level LoRM value.

render.description: Overrides the extraction rule for matching modules.
render.benefits: Lets one module group use a different rank-selection strategy.
render.drawbacks: Its parameter meaning changes with the selected mode.

normalizations.description: LoRMConfig first fills an omitted module override from the corresponding top-level LoRM value.

interactions.description: Its interpretation is selected by the module rule's extraction mode.

render.description: Overrides the numeric extraction parameter for matching modules.
render.benefits: Tunes compression separately for a module family.
render.drawbacks: An unsuitable value can retain too much or too little rank.

normalizations.description: LoRMConfig first fills an omitted module override from the corresponding top-level LoRM value.

render.description: Overrides the parameter-count eligibility threshold for matching modules.
render.benefits: Skips small modules within the matched family.
render.drawbacks: A high threshold can remove intended adaptation targets.

render.description: Attaches differential full-weight modules to remaining eligible non-linear/non-convolution leaves.
render.benefits: Can adapt weight-bearing layers outside the usual LoRA targets.
render.drawbacks: It greatly increases trainable parameters and checkpoint size.

render.description: Sets the base network scaling alpha.
render.benefits: Controls effective update scale independently of rank.
render.drawbacks: A poor alpha-to-rank relationship can weaken or exaggerate updates.

render.description: Sets convolution rank; null leaves convolution adaptation disabled unless another network mode forces it.
render.benefits: Adds capacity for convolution features.
render.drawbacks: It increases parameters and is unsupported or unnecessary for some architectures.

interactions.description: It inherits conv when omitted.

render.description: Sets convolution alpha, inheriting convolution rank when omitted.
render.benefits: Tunes convolution update scaling separately.
render.drawbacks: A mismatched scale can over- or under-emphasize convolution updates.

render.description: Sets network dropout when supported by the selected implementation.
render.benefits: Can regularize a high-capacity network.
render.drawbacks: Too much dropout slows learning or removes useful signal.

render.description: Enables network layer offloading during training.
render.benefits: Can reduce resident memory for supported network workflows.
render.drawbacks: Offloading adds transfers and cannot be merged in every save path.

interactions.description: It inherits alpha when omitted.

render.description: Sets linear-module alpha, inheriting the base alpha when omitted.
render.benefits: Tunes linear update scaling separately.
render.drawbacks: A mismatched scale can over- or under-emphasize linear updates.

interactions.description: This setting affects construction only for the LoKr network type.

render.description: Sets the LoKr factor; minus one requests automatic largest-factor selection.
render.benefits: Controls LoKr decomposition shape.
render.drawbacks: An unsuitable factor can fail shape construction or reduce useful capacity.

normalizations.description: When true for LoKr, linear/conv dimensions and alphas are overwritten with a full-rank sentinel.

interactions.description: This setting affects construction only for the LoKr network type.

render.description: For LoKr, forces effectively full-rank dimensions and alphas.
render.benefits: Maximizes LoKr representational capacity.
render.drawbacks: It sharply increases parameter count and memory use.

render.description: Provides nested LoRM extraction configuration.
render.benefits: Enables module-specific low-rank extraction behavior.
render.drawbacks: LoRM changes network construction and requires careful extraction rules.

render.description: Carries explicitly supported advanced arguments to the active first-party network constructor.
render.benefits: Exposes fine-grained target, rank-dropout, and module-shape controls.
render.drawbacks: Unknown or engine-reserved keys are rejected by the documented active dispatch boundary.

render.description: Requests the legacy LoKr naming/serialization behavior when the base model permits it.
render.benefits: Supports compatibility with older LoKr checkpoints.
render.drawbacks: Legacy format choices can reduce interoperability with current tooling.

render.description: Loads a local network checkpoint as the initial network state when no later resume checkpoint wins.
render.benefits: Supports refinement or continuation from existing LoRA weights.
render.drawbacks: A missing path is reported and ignored; incompatible weights can fail loading.

render.description: Records the historical multi-stage LoRA splitting switch.
render.benefits: Preserves configuration compatibility while the field remains accepted.
render.drawbacks: The current core process does not consume this parsed value.

render.description: Restricts network attachment to transformer-side modules where supported.
render.benefits: Avoids adapting other model components.
render.drawbacks: It can omit useful targets for architectures that need broader adaptation.

normalizations.description: LoRM forces linear/rank to 4 and forces conv to 4 when LoRM convolution extraction is enabled.

render.description: Selects the network implementation family.
render.benefits: Chooses LoRA, LoCon, LoRM, or LoKr construction behavior.
render.drawbacks: Changing type changes supported parameters and checkpoint compatibility.

normalizations.description: Legacy rank wins when present; otherwise linear is used; when both are omitted the effective rank is 4.

aliases.migration: Rename rank to linear; if both remain, the legacy rank value takes precedence.

render.description: Sets the low-rank dimension for linear modules.
render.benefits: Controls the primary tradeoff between adapter capacity and size.
render.drawbacks: Higher rank increases memory, training time, and checkpoint size; low rank may underfit.

render.description: Records the historical attention-only switch accepted by the active constructor.
render.benefits: Preserves compatibility with configurations that still carry the field.
render.drawbacks: The current constructor does not use the value to filter modules.

interactions.description: Alpha entries correspond positionally to block_dims.

render.description: Supplies per-block alpha values paired with block dimensions.
render.benefits: Tunes update scaling independently for each selected block.
render.drawbacks: Length or ordering mismatches with block dimensions produce invalid or unintended shapes.

render.description: Supplies per-block ranks for linear and 1x1 convolution targets.
render.benefits: Allocates network capacity differently across model blocks.
render.drawbacks: Large ranks increase memory and size; list shape must match the architecture.

interactions.description: Alpha entries correspond positionally to conv_block_dims.

render.description: Supplies per-block alpha values for 3x3 convolution targets.
render.benefits: Tunes convolution scaling by model block.
render.drawbacks: It requires matching convolution block dimensions and architecture ordering.

render.description: Supplies per-block ranks for 3x3 convolution targets.
render.benefits: Allocates convolution capacity by block.
render.drawbacks: It increases parameters and must align with convolution block alphas.

normalizations.description: A single string is converted to a one-element list; null becomes an empty list.

render.description: Replaces matching weighted leaf modules with full-weight modules instead of ordinary LoRA modules.
render.benefits: Gives selected layers full adaptation capacity.
render.drawbacks: Matching broad substrings can greatly increase trainable parameters and checkpoint size.

render.description: Adds full training modules for supported network input and output layers.
render.benefits: Can adapt boundary projections that ordinary target replacement omits.
render.drawbacks: It adds full-weight parameters and may reduce checkpoint portability.

normalizations.description: Null becomes an empty exclusion list.

render.description: Skips candidate modules whose names contain any listed substring.
render.benefits: Removes unwanted or unstable targets from the network.
render.drawbacks: Broad filters can silently exclude most trainable layers.

render.description: Sets whole-module dropout probability for each LoRA module.
render.benefits: Regularizes by occasionally bypassing an adapter module.
render.drawbacks: High probability weakens training and increases stochastic variation.

render.description: Keeps candidate modules only when their names contain a listed substring.
render.benefits: Restricts adaptation to a deliberate subnetwork.
render.drawbacks: Overly narrow filters can leave few or no trainable modules.

render.description: Skips candidate modules whose parameter count is below the threshold.
render.benefits: Avoids spending adapter capacity on small layers.
render.drawbacks: A high threshold can remove important targets.

normalizations.description: Transformer-family networks force PEFT format unless legacy LoKr format is active; PEFT format sets alpha equal to rank.

render.description: Uses PEFT-style module names and scaling behavior.
render.benefits: Improves compatibility with PEFT-oriented checkpoints for supported architectures.
render.drawbacks: It changes key names and forces alpha to rank, affecting interoperability with legacy formats.

render.description: Sets rank-component dropout probability.
render.benefits: Regularizes individual low-rank components.
render.drawbacks: High values reduce effective capacity and slow learning.

render.description: Prints the list of skipped modules using the constructor's legacy misspelled key.
render.benefits: Helps diagnose target selection.
render.drawbacks: It can produce long output and the misspelled key is retained only for compatibility.

interactions.description: This option is consumed by the active LyCORIS/LoCon constructor.

render.description: Enables CP decomposition for eligible non-1x1 LoCon convolution modules.
render.benefits: Can reduce the parameter cost of convolution adaptation.
render.drawbacks: It changes module shape and checkpoint compatibility and applies only to eligible convolutions.

render.description: Selects the concrete adapter architecture variant used by adapter implementations.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of adapter type for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: An unsupported variant fails construction or is incompatible with the selected model.

render.description: Sets the channel width at each T2I-adapter stage.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of channels for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Widths that do not match the model produce shape errors and larger widths consume more memory.

render.description: Lists class names used by class-aware adapter workflows.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of class names for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Incorrect ordering or names mislabel class-conditioned data.

normalizations.description: When omitted, ip+ selects penultimate_hidden_states and other adapter types select last_hidden_state.

render.description: Selects which CLIP vision representation supplies adapter features.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of clip layer for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: The wrong representation can degrade conditioning or mismatch adapter weights.

render.description: Sets the chance that control input is replaced with noise during training.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of control image dropout for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: High dropout weakens control adherence; zero provides no dropout regularization.

render.description: Enables convolutional pooling of adapter embeddings.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of conv pooling for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Pooling changes embedding shape and must match the adapter implementation.

render.description: Sets the number of convolutional pooling stacks.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of conv pooling stacks for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: More stacks add capacity, memory use, and training cost.

render.description: Sets the spatial downscale factor used by the adapter.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of downscale factor for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: A factor inconsistent with model latent resolution causes shape or quality problems.

render.description: Restricts Flux adapter application to double-stream blocks.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of flux only double for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: It omits single-stream blocks and can reduce adapter reach.

render.description: Adds the inpainting input channel behavior expected by control adapters.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of has inpainting input for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Enabling it without matching data/model channels produces incompatible inputs.

render.description: Sets the feature dimension per iLoRA attention head.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of head dim for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Incompatible dimensions cause shape errors; large dimensions cost memory.

render.description: Appends the masked start frame for image-to-video adapter pretraining.

render.description: Enables iLoRA modules in down blocks.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of ilora down for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Disabling the stage reduces capacity and changes checkpoint structure.

render.description: Enables iLoRA modules in the middle block.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of ilora mid for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Disabling the stage reduces capacity and changes checkpoint structure.

render.description: Enables iLoRA modules in up blocks.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of ilora up for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Disabling the stage reduces capacity and changes checkpoint structure.

render.description: Points to adapter image inputs used by applicable workflows.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of image dir for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: A missing or mismatched directory leaves the adapter without expected images.

render.description: Selects the image-encoder architecture used by the adapter.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of image encoder arch for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Architecture and checkpoint must agree or loading fails.

render.description: Overrides the image-encoder checkpoint path.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of image encoder path for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: A missing or incompatible checkpoint prevents encoder loading.

render.description: Sets adapter input channel count.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of in channels for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: It must match prepared control inputs or tensor shapes fail.

render.description: Sets the chance of inverting an inpainting mask during training.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of invert inpaint mask chance for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: High values change mask semantics frequently and can confuse preservation behavior.

normalizations.description: A present object is parsed through NetworkConfig before use.

render.description: Provides nested network settings for control-LoRA adapters.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of lora config for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Invalid network settings fail nested NetworkConfig parsing or produce incompatible weights.

interactions.description: This setting is relevant when scaler training is enabled.

render.description: Merges a trained channel scaler into adapter weights on save.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of merge scaler for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Merged output is harder to resume as a separately trainable scaler.

render.description: Selects an existing adapter name or local path to load.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of name or path for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Incompatible weights or a missing path prevent initialization.

render.description: Sets how many model blocks are cloned for LLM adapter training.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of num cloned blocks for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: More cloned blocks sharply increase memory and parameter count.

render.description: Sets the number of control images expected per example.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of num control images for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Dataset and model inputs must supply the same count.

render.description: Sets the number of iLoRA attention heads.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of num heads for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: More heads change shapes and increase computation.

render.description: Sets residual blocks per T2I-adapter stage.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of num res blocks for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: More blocks add compute and capacity; checkpoint shapes must match.

normalizations.description: When omitted, type ip+ selects 16 tokens and type ip selects 4 tokens.

render.description: Sets the number of adapter conditioning tokens.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of num tokens for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Token count changes memory and checkpoint shapes and must match the adapter type.

render.description: Caps image size for Pixtral adapter preprocessing.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of pixtral max image size for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Large caps increase encoder memory; small caps discard detail.

render.description: Randomizes Pixtral image size during training.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of pixtral random image size for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: It adds scale variation but reduces exact batch-shape predictability.

render.description: Enables four-image composition for applicable vision adapters.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of quad image for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: It changes expected inputs and increases image-encoding work.

render.description: Quantizes the LLM used by applicable adapter workflows.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of quantize llm for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Quantization saves memory but can reduce fidelity or add backend constraints.

render.description: Sets SAFE adapter hidden channel width.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of safe channels for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Larger widths cost memory and must match saved weights.

render.description: Sets SAFE reducer channel width.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of safe reducer channels for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: An incompatible width causes shape mismatch and larger widths cost memory.

render.description: Sets the number of SAFE adapter tokens.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of safe tokens for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Token count changes conditioning shape and checkpoint compatibility.

interactions.description: This setting is relevant when scaler training is enabled.

render.description: Overrides learning rate for the trainable adapter scaler.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of scaler lr for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: An excessive scaler rate can destabilize its channel weights.

render.description: Sets sparse-autoencoder feature dimension for applicable adapters.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of sparse autoencoder dim for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Large dimensions increase memory; incompatible dimensions fail shape construction.

render.description: Sets the subpixel adapter downscale factor.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of subpixel downscale factor for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: It must match the intended spatial packing or shapes and quality suffer.

normalizations.description: A comma-separated string is split, trimmed, and emptied pieces are discarded.

render.description: Provides one or more fixed test image paths for adapter evaluation.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of test img path for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Missing files prevent fixed-image evaluation.

render.description: Selects the adapter text-encoder architecture.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of text encoder arch for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: It must match the configured checkpoint and adapter implementation.

render.description: Overrides the adapter text-encoder checkpoint path.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of text encoder path for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: A missing or incompatible checkpoint prevents loading.

render.description: Enables training of the configured adapter.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of train for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Leaving it false keeps the adapter out of the trainable adapter path.

render.description: Enables image-encoder parameter training.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of train image encoder for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: It raises memory use and can overfit a small image set.

interactions.description: This narrows or forces image-encoder training.

render.description: Restricts image-encoder training to positional embeddings.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of train only image encoder positional embedding for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: It offers very limited capacity and is only useful for targeted adaptation.

render.description: Enables training of the adapter channel scaler.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of train scaler for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: It adds a separate trainable component that needs an appropriate learning rate.

render.description: Sets the token that activates applicable adapter conditioning.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of trigger for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: A common or inconsistent trigger can entangle adapter behavior.

render.description: Sets the class name associated with the adapter trigger for masked-prior workflows.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of trigger class name for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: An incorrect class name gives the preservation target the wrong semantics.

render.description: Selects the top-level adapter family.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of type for compatible adapter workflows.
render.drawbacks: Each family requires different inputs, weights, and compatible model support.

render.description: Sets the square resolution used to cache and compare validation latents.
render.benefits: Makes resolution explicit for repeatable validation checks.
render.drawbacks: Higher resolution increases validation memory and time and must suit the model.

render.description: Sets the optimizer-step interval between validation loss evaluations.
render.benefits: Makes validate every n steps explicit for repeatable validation checks.
render.drawbacks: Short intervals add repeated validation work and slow training.

normalizations.description: Mapping items are converted to ValidationItem objects; existing ValidationItem objects are retained.

render.description: Lists fixed images and prompts used for validation.
render.benefits: Makes validation items explicit for repeatable validation checks.
render.drawbacks: Missing or invalid image items are skipped, and an empty usable list disables validation.

render.description: Lists noise sigma levels evaluated for each validation item.
render.benefits: Makes validation sigmas explicit for repeatable validation checks.
render.drawbacks: More sigma levels multiply validation work; unsuitable levels may not represent the training regime.

render.description: Points to the fixed image encoded for one validation case.
render.benefits: Makes each validation item's image path explicit and repeatable.
render.drawbacks: An empty or missing path causes the item to be skipped.

render.description: Sets the prompt paired with this validation image.
render.benefits: Makes each validation item's prompt explicit and repeatable.
render.drawbacks: A prompt unrelated to the image makes the validation loss harder to interpret.

render.description: Sets the source text used to initialize new embedding token vectors.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of embedding init words.
render.drawbacks: Poor initialization can slow convergence or bias the learned token toward an unrelated concept.

render.description: Chooses safetensors or PyTorch serialization for the learned embedding.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of embedding save format.
render.drawbacks: PyTorch and safetensors outputs target different consumers and have different safety properties.

render.description: Sets the number of trainable tokens allocated to the embedding.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of embedding tokens.
render.drawbacks: More tokens add capacity but make prompting and optimization more complex.

render.description: Sets the prompt trigger that expands to the learned embedding tokens.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of embedding trigger.
render.drawbacks: A common trigger can collide with existing vocabulary and entangle the concept.

render.description: Sets the class name used with the embedding trigger for inverted masked-prior behavior.
render.benefits: Provides explicit control of embedding trigger class name.
render.drawbacks: An incorrect class name gives preservation prompts the wrong semantic target.
